newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet seeks New Caledonia nickel talks.
newsitem.headline: Eramet seeks New Caledonia nickel talks.

text.p: Eramet, the world's third-biggest nickel producer, said on Thursday it wanted to meet with the management of Canadian group Falconbridge and Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) to discuss their plans to build a rival nickel plant in New Caledonia.
Chairman Yves Rambaud told a news conference he had sent a letter to the presidents of both companies, offering a meeting in mid-May and had tentatively proposed May 2 as the date.
Eramet made its offer of talks as its management faces considerable pressure from the French government over plans to distribute mining assets in the South Pacific island.
At a Thursday board meeting, state-holding Erap, which owns 55 percent of Eramet, said it wanted its representatives to hold a majority of seats on Eramet's board.
The request, if approved by a shareholders' meeting on May 29, would give the government a free hand in its long-standing dispute with Eramet.
Industry sources said the move could pave the way for the ouster of chairman Yves Rambaud, who opposes any plans to curtail Eramet's development in New Caledonia.
Eramet's board currently includes three Erap representatives and one member of state-controlled Bureau de Recherches Geologiques et Minieres (BRMG).
Rambaud declined to comment on Erap's proposal. But he said that Eramet's economic performance over the last three years proved that the group's strategy could hardly be challenged.
The French state has begun the process to remove Eramet's mining licence for the Koniambo mine in New Caledonia, saying Eramet did not operate the mine for 10 years.
Koniambo nickel ore reserves would be used to supply the plant Falconbridge and local Kanak group SMSP want to build in the north.
The project is part of a deal to appease Kanak separatists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence for the French territory.

Government came up with that plan after previous talks between Eramet and SMSP over an asset swap failed. Under that initial plan SMSP would get the right to use the Koniambo field and Eramet would obtain the rights for the Poum field.
Eramet has said it would use all legal means available to fight the plan to withdraw the Koniambo licence, arguing it was unjustified and would limit its development.
Rambaud said that he wanted all parties involved to sit down and work out a solution for building the plant in the north.
"We are ready to play a role. We have made positive proposals. But as long as all industrial players involved do not meet and talk, chances for success are nil," Rambaud said.

He said that future talks must clarify several issues, including how much ore would be needed to supply the new plant, how much SMSP would be able to provide and how much Eramet would need to bring in.
He said Eramet was ready to help supply the plant and also willing to work on the initial plan to swap assets with SMSP as long as the terms of the exchange were fair.
He said international experts must be brought in to assess possible compensation that must be paid Eramet if the exchange took place.
Eramet plans to expand nickel production in New Caledonia to 60,000-65,000 tonnes from the year 2000 from a current 54,000 tonnes.
